To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SLIT2 is a novel "therapeutic and prognostic factor" for lung cancer.

1) the expression level of SLIT2 is associated with poor survival of lung cancer patients; and 2) SLIT2 is a tumor suppressor gene that inhibits lung cancer progression through the AKT/Glycogen Synthase Kinase 3 beta/Beta-TrCP pathway.

SLIT2 is frequently down-regulated in lung cancer, that SLIT2 down-regulation is associated with lung cancer progression, and that SLIT2 can inhibit lung cancer cell migration by attenuating beta-catenin/E-cadherin.

the SLIT2 protein, which is a member of a family of extracellular glycoproteins.
the role of SLIT2 in lung cancer.
the role of the SLIT-ROBO signaling system in lung cancer progression.
